rituals.name: MAKE THE BELIEF BET
rituals.title: MAKE THE BELIEF BET
rituals.goal: Test a belief with a small action that could prove it wrong — aim current charge.
rituals.steps:
1. State the belief as a clear prediction.
2. Choose a safe, small action that could prove it wrong as well as right.
3. Picture the expected result before acting.
4. Run the test, then compare observation with prediction.
5. Pay out only to evidence.
rituals.winReward: Observation, not expectation, decided how the belief's prediction scored after the experiment.
rituals.win: Observation, not expectation, decided how the belief's prediction scored after the experiment.
rituals.mindBend: A belief that never risks disconfirmation can feel strong simply because it has never been allowed to lose.
rituals.formulaFlow: State Belief → Choose Safe → Picture Outcome → Test Observation → Pay Out

rituals.name: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
rituals.title: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
rituals.goal: Start at the smallest task level that still leaves real evidence; channel useful momentum.
rituals.steps:
1. Name five versions of the task from almost easy to genuinely stretching.
2. Mentally remove the zero-effort decoy.
3. Do the smallest remaining version that leaves visible evidence—one paragraph, one call, one plate washed.
4. Next time, climb only one stair.
rituals.winReward: One visible piece of work existed, and the next challenge only needed to rise by one step.
rituals.win: One visible piece of work existed, and the next challenge only needed to rise by one step.
rituals.mindBend: The useful starting point is not zero effort or maximum effort — it is the smallest dose that leaves proof behind.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name → Remove Decoy → Remain Version → Climb Stair

PAUSE
Reduce the step further if illness, exhaustion, or overload is being ignored.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: MOOD HAS ALIBIS
rituals.title: MOOD HAS ALIBIS
rituals.goal: Redirect useful drive: compare predicted mood with what actually changes during real activities.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose one activity.
2. Before it, score expected mood; at the start, notice your actual mood; at the end, score again.
3. Add one sentence about what changed during the activity.
4. Repeat with three different actions before deciding ‘nothing helps.’
rituals.winReward: Several activities produced before-and-after evidence before the claim 'nothing helps' was allowed to stand.
rituals.win: Several activities produced before-and-after evidence before the claim 'nothing helps' was allowed to stand.
rituals.mindBend: Mood predicts its own future badly. Action can create data that the current feeling cannot imagine in advance.
rituals.formulaFlow: Choose Activity → Score Expected → Add Sentence → Try Ways
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek professional support if low mood is severe, persistent, or linked to self-harm thoughts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: TWO ENGINES
rituals.title: TWO ENGINES
rituals.goal: Feed pleasure and mastery separately instead of asking one activity to fix everything — steady useful momentum.
rituals.steps:
1. For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence.
2. Make both small enough to happen.
3. After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only.
4. Do not demand that either activity fix everything.
rituals.winReward: One small enjoyable act and one competence-building act each delivered evidence to their own channel.
rituals.win: One small enjoyable act and one competence-building act each delivered evidence to their own channel.
rituals.mindBend: Pleasure and mastery are different engines; a day can regain traction even when only one of them starts.
rituals.formulaFlow: Schedule Chosen → Make Small → Check Both → Drop Demand

rituals.name: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
rituals.title: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
rituals.goal: Guide rising drive; make the wanted behaviour easier to enter and the unwanted default harder to reach.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick one desired behaviour and one unwanted default.
2. Picture the desired route becoming easier and the unwanted route becoming slightly harder.
3. Imagine one extra decision appearing before the unwanted default can happen.
4. Mentally rehearse taking the easier desired route once.
rituals.winReward: The environment contained an extra pause before the old default and a smoother route toward the desired action.
rituals.win: The environment contained an extra pause before the old default and a smoother route toward the desired action.
rituals.mindBend: Willpower is not the only voter. Friction quietly decides many behaviours before motivation gets a turn.
rituals.formulaFlow: Pick Desired → Picture Routes → Add Friction → Let Choice

rituals.name: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
rituals.title: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
rituals.ritual_name: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
rituals.goal: Let an urge rise and fall without doing the usual ritual; channel high charge.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the cue and the usual calming act it normally summons.
2. Contact only a manageable dose of the cue.
3. Keep your hands and attention out of the ritual while the urge changes on its own.
4. Hold the peak and the first natural drop.
5. The learning comes from not doing the old ritual.
rituals.winReward: The urge changed on its own while the old calming act stayed undone.
rituals.win: The urge changed on its own while the old calming act stayed undone.
rituals.mindBend: An urge learns it is survivable when it peaks without being paid off by the ritual.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Cue → Contact → Keep Hands → Mark Peak → Let Learning

rituals.name: BODY VETO
rituals.title: BODY VETO
rituals.goal: Pace extra surge: break the automatic reach by putting your body in a deliberate opposite position.
rituals.steps:
1. Spot the first motor cue—reaching, picking, scrolling, biting, clenching.
2. Use a safe opposite posture and practise it slowly three times.
3. When the cue appears, enter that posture for ten seconds while naming the urge.
4. Then decide consciously.
rituals.winReward: The first motor cue appeared, and your body paused long enough for a conscious choice.
rituals.win: The first motor cue appeared, and your body paused long enough for a conscious choice.
rituals.mindBend: Choice can enter through posture before the mind has finished arguing with the impulse.
rituals.formulaFlow: Identify Motor → Choose Safe → Enter Posture → Decide Consciously
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
rituals.title: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
rituals.goal: Aim useful drive; watch a craving as a changing curve before deciding what protects the next hour.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice its current level and where it moves in the body.
2. Watch for slope: rising, flattening, cresting, falling.
3. Every thirty seconds, imagine the next point without acting on the urge.
4. When the line changes direction, name the change.
5. Choose what protects the next hour.
rituals.winReward: You noticed the urge's slope change without acting at its peak.
rituals.win: You noticed the urge's slope change without acting at its peak.
rituals.mindBend: A craving feels like a command when you see only its height. Watching its slope reveals that it is moving.

rituals.name: COOL THE ALARM PANEL
rituals.title: COOL THE ALARM PANEL
rituals.goal: Pace current energy; use brief comfortable coolness as a reset cue, not a toughness test.
rituals.steps:
1. Use cool—not painfully cold—water or a wrapped cool pack on the cheeks and around the eyes for a brief interval.
2. Slow your body while the sensation lands.
3. Remove it, name the room, and reassess the next safe action.
4. Treat the cool sensation as a reset cue. Stop before it becomes an endurance test.

rituals.name: THE LONGER OUT-BREATH
rituals.title: THE LONGER OUT-BREATH
rituals.goal: Harness rising charge: lengthen the out-breath gently, then make one workable decision from a steadier pace.
rituals.steps:
1. Breathe in without pulling extra air.
2. Let the outflow last slightly longer, as though fogging a distant window silently.
3. Repeat only while comfortable; keep shoulders quiet and jaw loose.
4. After several rounds, resume natural breathing and look for one workable decision.
rituals.winReward: Breathing returned to normal and one next decision looked usable rather than urgent.

rituals.name: STAY FOR THE UPDATE
rituals.title: STAY FOR THE UPDATE
rituals.goal: Stay with a manageable fear cue long enough to notice reality contradict one prediction — guide high charge.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose an external cue low enough on your fear ladder to approach voluntarily.
2. Enter without escape and remain until you observe at least one mismatch between prediction and reality.
3. Name the mismatch before leaving.
4. Repeat later under safe conditions rather than chasing maximum distress.
rituals.winReward: You left after naming one mismatch between what you expected and what actually occurred.
rituals.win: You left after naming one mismatch between what you expected and what actually occurred.

rituals.name: PUT THE DATE BACK IN
rituals.title: PUT THE DATE BACK IN
rituals.goal: Guide extra surge; separate a memory alarm from the current moment using only present-day facts.
rituals.steps:
1. With both eyes open, state the calendar date and say where you are.
2. Name three ordinary objects you can see without describing the memory.
3. Press both feet down and point toward the nearest safe exit.
4. Say, ‘That was then; I am here now,’ then choose one neutral task.
rituals.winReward: Those present-day cues made it easier to find where you are now and choose what comes next.
rituals.win: Those present-day cues made it easier to find where you are now and choose what comes next.
rituals.mindBend: A memory alarm can feel current without being current. Time, place, and action cues give the brain a present-tense timestamp.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Date → Name Place → Find Exit → Choose Present
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep both eyes open and stay with present-day facts only. Do not revisit, describe, or visualise the traumatic memory. Stop if you feel unreal, disconnected, overwhelmed, or less sure where you are, and connect with qualified human support.
This is present-day grounding only, not trauma treatment.

rituals.name: LEAVE ONE QUESTION OPEN
rituals.title: LEAVE ONE QUESTION OPEN
rituals.goal: Redirect current impulse: leave one low-stakes question unanswered until a chosen review time.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose a low-stakes unknown.
2. Picture it on a card and forbid checking, asking, or mentally solving until a set time.
3. Carry the unanswered card while doing normal life.
4. At review, notice what the urge did—not whether certainty arrived.

rituals.win: Normal life continued while the urge to solve or check changed on its own.

rituals.name: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
rituals.title: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
rituals.goal: Remain with a safe practice cue through the first signs of recovery, then end deliberately — slow hot impulse.
rituals.steps:
1. During a safe practice round, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
2. Do not leave at that first relief.
3. Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
4. Departure follows learning, not panic.
rituals.winReward: You stayed past the first relief until your gaze, movement, or urge showed visible recovery.

display.title: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
display.goal: Remain with a safe practice cue through the first signs of recovery, then end deliberately — slow hot impulse.
display.numberedSteps:
1. During a safe practice round, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
2. Do not leave at that first relief.
3. Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
4. Departure follows learning, not panic.
display.win: You stayed past the first relief until your gaze, movement, or urge showed visible recovery.
display.mindBend: Leaving at the first dip can teach 'escape worked'; staying into recovery lets the body learn 'the wave changed here'.
display.formulaFlow: Highest → Stay Past → Remain Cue → Exit Recovered

rituals.name: REMOVE ONE INVISIBLE CRUTCH
rituals.title: REMOVE ONE INVISIBLE CRUTCH
rituals.goal: Drop one unnecessary safety habit while keeping real safety intact; slow high speed.
rituals.steps:

2. Drop only that act while keeping legitimate safety intact.
3. Observe what the outcome says without it.

rituals.win: The practice continued without one protective crutch, giving you evidence about what happened in its absence.

rituals.name: MOVE THE LESSON
rituals.title: MOVE THE LESSON
rituals.goal: Redirect raw drive: carry a learned skill into changing conditions instead of trusting it only in one setting.
rituals.steps:
1. Repeat a mastered practice while changing one feature: location, time, cue order, duration, or intensity.
2. On the next round, alter a different feature.
3. Keep a small mental map of where the skill still works.
4. Let variation turn a local success into portable knowledge.
rituals.winReward: The skill still worked after at least one feature of the context was deliberately changed.
rituals.win: The skill still worked after at least one feature of the context was deliberately changed.
rituals.mindBend: Learning becomes portable when it survives variation — otherwise the brain may file success under one room, time, or cue.
rituals.formulaFlow: Repeat Mastered → Change Again → Map Transfer → Make Portable

rituals.name: THE TWO-CUE MERGE
rituals.title: THE TWO-CUE MERGE
rituals.goal: Combine two manageable triggers and compare the real effect with what you predicted — contain sharp surge.
rituals.steps:
1. Select two triggers already manageable separately.
2. Predict what joining them will add.
3. Contact both at a modest dose while dropping unnecessary escape.
4. Stay long enough to compare the combined result with the prediction, then recover fully.
rituals.winReward: Both cues were present together long enough to reveal whether their combined impact matched the forecast.
rituals.win: Both cues were present together long enough to reveal whether their combined impact matched the forecast.
rituals.mindBend: Two familiar triggers do not automatically create twice the danger. Combination is another prediction that reality can test.
rituals.formulaFlow: Select Triggers → Predict Joining → Drop Unnecessary → Stay Long

rituals.name: TAKE SAFETY ON TOUR
rituals.title: TAKE SAFETY ON TOUR
rituals.goal: Pace useful momentum; use an already-learned skill in a different safe setting and see what transfers.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick a different secure setting for a skill already learned elsewhere.
2. Before entering, recall the earlier evidence in one sentence.
3. Practise, notice what transfers, and spot any context-specific obstacle.
4. Leave with a local reminder for next time.
rituals.winReward: Old evidence travelled with you, while one local obstacle or useful carryover became clear.
rituals.win: Old evidence travelled with you, while one local obstacle or useful carryover became clear.
rituals.mindBend: Confidence tied to a place can look like a personal weakness; changing the setting tests whether the learning was actually broader.

rituals.name: TURN UP THE WHISPER
rituals.title: TURN UP THE WHISPER
rituals.goal: Amplify one tiny spontaneous body tendency just enough to learn what it is asking for; steady hot rush.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice the smallest spontaneous tendency: sway, curl, stretch, turn, reach.
2. Enlarge it by only ten percent and pause.
3. Check if it brings ease, protection, energy, or nothing.
4. Let the answer determine whether to continue, reverse, or stop.
rituals.winReward: A small sway, curl, stretch, turn, or reach became clearer and showed whether it brought ease, protection, energy, or nothing.
rituals.win: A small sway, curl, stretch, turn, or reach became clearer and showed whether it brought ease, protection, energy, or nothing.
rituals.mindBend: The body often whispers before it shouts. Increasing a signal slightly can make its direction readable without forcing it.
rituals.formulaFlow: Smallest → Pause Enlarge → Ask Whether → Let Determine

rituals.name: DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT
rituals.title: DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT
rituals.goal: Anchor to today's date using the room, an exit, and reachable support — harness extra rush.
rituals.steps:
1. Say today's full date and your current location aloud.
2. Read the names of three ordinary objects directly in front of you.
3. Point to the nearest safe exit without moving toward the past memory.
4. Name one person or service available in the present.
5. Keep eyes open and return attention to the whole room.
rituals.winReward: Today's date, current location, ordinary objects, a safe exit, and a present-day helper all became explicit.
rituals.win: Today's date, current location, ordinary objects, a safe exit, and a present-day helper all became explicit.
rituals.mindBend: Trauma memory can erase timestamps. Ordinary present facts act like metadata the alarm response did not carry with it.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Date → Read Objects → Locate Exit → Name Support → Return Room
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open. Use only present-day room, date, place and support orientation. Do not revisit memories in detail, use trauma imagery, intensify sensations, or attempt unsupervised processing. Stop for flooding, feeling unreal or disconnected, or weakened orientation and connect with qualified human support.
This is grounding only, not trauma treatment.

rituals.name: WHAT REMAINS WHEN REWARD LEAVES?
rituals.title: WHAT REMAINS WHEN REWARD LEAVES?
rituals.goal: Pace current speed; find the responsibility that remains even when reward, praise, and punishment disappear.
rituals.steps:
1. Name your role, the people affected, and the values governing it.
2. Mentally remove applause, punishment, and personal advantage.
3. Ask which responsibility still stands.
4. Convert that answer into a time-bound action and one limit on what the role does not require.
rituals.winReward: One value-based duty survived the removal of personal advantage and became a time-bound action with a clear limit.
rituals.win: One value-based duty survived the removal of personal advantage and became a time-bound action with a clear limit.
rituals.mindBend: A responsibility that vanishes without applause may have been serving reward more than values. What remains reveals the deeper contract.

rituals.name: NO-CONCEPT MINUTE
rituals.title: NO-CONCEPT MINUTE

rituals.steps:
1. Set a brief interval.
2. During it, do not create causes, labels, comparisons, or solutions.
3. Attend to direct colour, sound, contact, and movement.
4. If a concept appears, acknowledge ‘explanation’ and let the sensory world continue.
rituals.winReward: Colour, sound, contact, and movement continued while labels, comparisons, and solutions were treated as later additions.
rituals.win: Colour, sound, contact, and movement continued while labels, comparisons, and solutions were treated as later additions.
rituals.mindBend: Explanation can arrive so fast that direct experience becomes background; removing concepts briefly shows what was there before the commentary.
rituals.formulaFlow: Set Brief → Name Comparisons → Attend Direct → Let Sensory

rituals.name: WIDEN THE PRESENT CAMERA
rituals.title: WIDEN THE PRESENT CAMERA
rituals.goal: Widen your view of the current room when a memory feels too close; steady high charge.
rituals.steps:
1. Rest your eyes on a plain object and name its colour.
2. Shift to a second object farther away and name its shape.
3. Turn your head slowly and identify the room’s widest visible edge.
4. Say your current location and choose the next ordinary action.
rituals.winReward: Attention moved from one close cue to the wider room and a present-day action.
rituals.win: Attention moved from one close cue to the wider room and a present-day action.
rituals.mindBend: When attention narrows, a memory can fill the frame. Widening the real visual field gives the present more space.
rituals.formulaFlow: Fix Object → Shift Farther → Widen Room → Choose Action
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open and use only the room that is actually around you. Do not picture, revisit, or change the memory. Stop if you feel unreal, disconnected, overwhelmed, or less oriented, and connect with qualified human support.
This is present-day grounding only, not trauma treatment.

display.title: ASK WHAT THE MEMORY IS STILL BILLING
display.goal: Find what a memory is still demanding and route that demand to the right present response; find useful traction.
display.numberedSteps:

3. Route the claim to BOUNDARY, REPAIR, GRIEF, or IMPOSSIBLE REVERSAL. Do not create a fifth category.
4. Choose the matching present response: set protection, request safe repair, make room for grief, or stop billing today for a reversal history cannot provide.
display.win: The claim became boundary, repair, grief, or impossible reversal, and the next action matched that category.
display.mindBend: Rumination often sends every unpaid emotional bill to thinking. Some debts need protection, repair, grief, or acceptance rather than another analysis lap.

display.goal: Aim raw charge: plan from what is likely and supported, not from what is merely possible.
display.numberedSteps:

rituals.name: THIS IS A CHAPTER, NOT THE BOOK
rituals.title: THIS IS A CHAPTER, NOT THE BOOK
rituals.ritual_name: THIS IS A CHAPTER, NOT THE BOOK
rituals.goal: Guide raw charge: put today's event inside a much longer life story instead of making it the title.

rituals.title: CALL THE MENTAL MEETING TO ORDER
rituals.ritual_name: CALL THE MENTAL MEETING TO ORDER
rituals.goal: Redirect extra speed: give each mental topic a purpose, time allowance, and evidence requirement before it gets discussion time.
rituals.steps:

2. Order by consequence and deadline.
3. Process only the first item; place every interruption in the parking lot for its scheduled turn.

rituals.name: NOTICE THE SPACE DOING THE HOLDING
rituals.title: NOTICE THE SPACE DOING THE HOLDING
rituals.ritual_name: NOTICE THE SPACE DOING THE HOLDING
rituals.goal: Guide sharp rush; make the empty space around and between things as noticeable as the things themselves.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine three simple forms.
2. Notice the space inside openings, around edges, and between the forms.
3. Reverse figure and ground until space feels as noticeable as matter.
4. Include the sense of room around your body.
rituals.winReward: Figure and ground reversed until openings, gaps, and room around the body had equal perceptual weight.
rituals.win: Figure and ground reversed until openings, gaps, and room around the body had equal perceptual weight.
rituals.mindBend: Attention treats objects as content and space as nothing, even though space is part of every shape you can see.
rituals.formulaFlow: Choose Forms → Attend Space → Reverse Figure → Include Room

rituals.name: LET THE WATCHER GO TOO
rituals.title: LET THE WATCHER GO TOO
rituals.goal: Aim sharp impulse: notice the feeling of being ‘the watcher’ without having to keep that position in place.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice the subtle feeling that says ‘I am the observer’.
2. Treat that feeling or location as another experience you can notice.
3. Let awareness continue without holding a separate watcher in place.
4. Return to an ordinary action straight afterward.
rituals.winReward: The effort of being the observer was noticed, then ordinary awareness continued without holding that position.
rituals.win: The effort of being the observer was noticed, then ordinary awareness continued without holding that position.
rituals.mindBend: Trying to be the observer can become another identity. Awareness does not need a separate manager standing outside experience.
rituals.formulaFlow: Notice Watcher → Notice Position → Release Watcher → Return Action

PAUSE
Do not attempt when self-experience is unstable or unreal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: CHANGE THE SYMBOL’S JOB
rituals.title: CHANGE THE SYMBOL’S JOB
rituals.goal: Change one feature of the symbol carrying the state, then turn any inner shift into action; contain current surge.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine one symbol that represents the state.
2. Open it, cool it, soften it, widen it, or give it an edge.
3. Notice what changes inside as the symbol changes.
4. Turn that inner shift into one practical next move.
rituals.winReward: The symbol softened, opened, cooled, widened, or gained an edge, and one practical move followed the change.
rituals.win: The symbol softened, opened, cooled, widened, or gained an edge, and one practical move followed the change.

rituals.name: THE LIVABLE OPTION
rituals.title: THE LIVABLE OPTION
rituals.goal: State your own view before letting another person's opinion back into the decision; shape sharp surge.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice whose opinion is taking up the most space in your head.
2. Name your own view before comparing it with theirs.
3. Say your choice in one plain sentence.
4. Check it against the earliest deadline or consequence that truly matters.
5. Decide what belongs to this decision now and what can wait.
rituals.winReward: The choice was checked against a real deadline or consequence and only the part belonging to now stayed active.
rituals.win: The choice was checked against a real deadline or consequence and only the part belonging to now stayed active.
rituals.mindBend: External opinion is easiest to mistake for your own preference when your own view has never been spoken first.
rituals.formulaFlow: Check Capacity → Sort Now → Sample It → Name Due → Current

keywords: You are trying to suppress an intrusive thought

display.title: LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN
display.goal: Stop fighting the thought and continue one small task without checking whether it left — channel sharp surge.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Say, “This thought is allowed to be here for this minute.”
2. Notice one sound or object outside your head without using it to escape or prove anything.
3. Start one small task while letting the thought remain in the background.
4. Do not check whether the thought has faded before continuing.
display.win: The thought was allowed in the background while action continued without a disappearance check.
display.mindBend: Suppression gives a thought a monitoring job: keep searching for it to confirm it is gone. Permission ends that hidden task.
display.formulaFlow: Allow Thought → Notice Outside → Start Task → Skip Check

safety.raw:
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.
